html:
The Annals is a history of the Roman emperors from the death of Augustus in 14 to the death of Nero in 68, written by the senator Tacitus around 116 or later. It was his last work and is usually thought his best.

Tacitus writes year by year, but his real subject is power: how Tiberius, Claudius and Nero ruled, and how senators flattered, informed on each other and died. His style is short, dark and full of sharp asides. He claimed to write "without anger or bias", yet his view of the emperors is grim.

Only about half survives. The books on Caligula are lost, as is the end of Nero's reign. What remains includes the Great Fire of Rome of 64 and Nero's punishment of Christians, with one of the earliest non-Christian mentions of Christ. Together with Suetonius, the Annals shapes almost everything we picture about the early empire.
sum: The Annals is a history of the Roman emperors from the death of Augustus in 14 to the death of Nero in 68, written by the senator Tacitus around 116 or later. It was his last work and is usually thought his best.
